learningObjectives: Name the five tabs of the Message section and what each one shows.
Explain why testing directly in the API Scan (before exporting) is valuable.
Create an item via POST and verify it via GET within the same API Scan session.
Rename Messages to reflect their function ahead of exporting to Tosca.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: The Five Tabs of the Message Section

rows: The request or response message itself. On first load it's a structural template; fill it in to send real data.
The HTTP Method used for the request (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE...). If Method is GET, the Payload may be empty depending on the SUT.
The resource identifier for this endpoint.
Displays and edits parameters, such as the "key" Service Access Key.

elements.title: Additional tabs
items: Authentication tab — for services requiring authentication configuration beyond a simple key parameter.
Attachments tab — displays and edits attachments, e.g. sending an image when testing an API that generates new user profiles with profile pictures.
Header section — shows either the request or response Headers, depending on which message view is currently selected.

elements.text: It's valuable to test directly in the API Scan before exporting anything to Tosca: this is where you discover the real default values returned by the server, which you'll need later as genuine test data in the exported TestCase. Modifications to a Message can also be made right here if a result isn't what you expect.

bulletPoints: Payload is the main working area; Method/Endpoint/Resource/Params/Authentication/Attachments/Header are supporting tabs.
Testing in the API Scan first surfaces real server data you'll reuse as test values after exporting.

elements.title: Verify the shop list, add a shop, verify again
items: In Shops_Get (inside the "shops" folder), set the "key" parameter to your Service Access Key. The Payload should be empty by default for this GET.
Send the request — the Response lists every shop/branch currently in the system.
Switch to Shops_Post, re-confirm the key parameter, then edit the Payload with the new shop's details, respecting the existing quotation marks and colon syntax.
Send the request — the view switches to Response mode; a 200 OK status code confirms the addition.
Send Shops_Get again to confirm the new shop now appears — by default, new entries appear last in the list.

elements.text: These Business Parameters (Business-relevant elements of a message, such as name, ID or address) work in a similar fashion to Business Parameters in a Tosca TestCase — but they are attached to the API Scan payload, not a Reusable TestStepBlock.

bulletPoints: GET first to see what already exists, POST to add, GET again to confirm — a repeatable verification pattern.
Respect existing JSON syntax (quotes, colons) exactly when editing the Payload by hand.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing the Method tab with the HTTP verb in the Payload
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates look for the HTTP Method (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) inside the Payload tab instead of the dedicated Method tab.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Method tab specifically identifies the HTTP Method used for the request. The Payload tab holds the message content/body, which can be empty for some GET requests depending on the SUT.

examPitfalls.title: Skipping verification directly in the API Scan
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates export straight to Tosca without first sending requests in the API Scan to see real server responses.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Testing directly in the API Scan surfaces the actual default values returned by the server — valuable real test data to reuse once the Message is exported into a Tosca TestCase.

examPitfalls.title: Breaking JSON syntax when editing the Payload
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates add new values to the Payload but misplace quotation marks or colons, breaking the JSON structure.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When manually editing values in the Payload, keep new content between the pre-existing quotation marks and after the colon exactly as the surrounding syntax expects.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which tab in the API Scan's Message section shows the HTTP Method used for the request?
practiceQuiz.hint: This tab is named exactly after what it shows.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Method tab identifies the HTTP Method used for the request (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.). In some cases, if the Method is GET, the Payload can be empty.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which tab would you use to send an image while testing an API that creates new user profiles with profile pictures?
practiceQuiz.hint: This tab is specifically for files sent alongside a message.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Attachments tab displays and edits attachments, such as an image sent to test an API's capability to generate new user profiles including profile pictures.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why is it valuable to test a Message directly in the API Scan before exporting it to Tosca?

options.text: Because the API Scan cannot export Messages that haven't been sent at least once.
Because testing there reveals the real default values returned by the server, which become useful test data later.
Because Tosca cannot connect to REST APIs directly.
It isn't valuable — exporting first and testing afterward is always faster.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what you gain by seeing an actual server response before building the TestCase.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Testing directly in the API Scan surfaces real default values returned by the server — for example an address or an ID — which come in handy later as genuine test data in the exported TestCase.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester wants to confirm a complete list of shops without modifying any data. Which HTTP Method should the Message use?
practiceQuiz.hint: This method retrieves data without changing anything on the server.
practiceQuiz.rationale: GET requests data from a specified resource without modifying it — the correct choice for retrieving the complete, unmodified list of shops.

quickRecap.value: Payload, Method, Endpoint, Resource, Params, Authentication, Attachments, Header.
The message body — template on first load, editable before sending.
Shows the HTTP verb (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) used by the request.
Reveals real server default values you'll reuse as test data after exporting to Tosca.
GET (see current state) → POST (add) → GET again (confirm the addition).
